items.message: The change does what it says: it expands the required review check from one lens to all four shipped lenses, adds failure-isolation so one lens cannot suppress the others, shares a single cassette across all four runs, and updates the cost commentary to reflect the new per-push spend. The workflow change matches the description exactly.

The test file discharges GATE-REVIEW-5 as described. It checks both directions (bound lens not run, name in loop not bound), adds a positive control against vacuity, and verifies the failure-isolation and single-cassette properties by inspecting the workflow YAML directly. All four assertions correspond to claims made in the PR description and the gate ledger entry.

GATE-REVIEW-5 is added and its prose matches the implementation: the comparison is against `_review_lenses` over the loaded module, both directions are asserted, and the scoping note (this repository only, not what `init` scaffolds) is reflected in the scaffold comment added to `cli.py`.
O9 and O10 rows are updated to reference GATE-REVIEW-5. Both additions are consistent with the gate ledger entry and the workflow change. No other objective rows are touched.

The scaffold comments added to the GitHub Actions and GitLab CI templates explain that one lens is scaffolded rather than four, and point the adopter to `in-lockstep ls`. This matches the description's stated scoping decision (quadrupling a stranger's first bill is not ours to make). No functional scaffold code is changed — only comments.

Minor gap worth noting: `test_the_lenses_share_one_tape_so_the_harvest_sees_them_all` counts `--cassette` occurrences in the `run` string, but the `run` block also contains inline comments that could in principle mention `--cassette` in prose. This is low risk today (the comments do not), but the assertion would pass even if a second `--cassette` appeared in a comment rather than a real invocation.
